_meta.source_document: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Urban District, Karnataka State (2022)
_meta.extraction_method: pdftotext -layout on machine-readable (born-digital) PDF; three headline tables (Hazardous, Bio-Medical, C&D) additionally rendered at 200 dpi (pdftoppm) and read as images to confirm every numeric figure.
_meta.page_label_convention: Citations use the document's printed footer label ('Page | N'), matching the convention used in the sibling bengaluru-urban-dep.json (which cites e.g. p.78). The printed label N equals PDF page N+3 (cover + 2 front-matter pages precede printed p.1).
_meta.scope_note: All three streams (hazardous, biomedical, C&D) are reported DISTRICT-wide in this DEP. BBMP (Bengaluru city corporation) is the dominant generator in every stream and is the only ULB with named recycling/treatment infrastructure. Yelahanka is not broken out as a separate ULB in these tables - it falls within BBMP limits; the only Yelahanka-specific mention in these sections is the Mavallipura dumpsite (a contaminated site) at Yelahanka, Bengaluru-560064.

figures.integrated_TSDF: Nil (no integrated Transport-Storage-Disposal Facility in district)
figures.contaminated_or_probable_contaminated_si: 1 (Mavallipura dumpsite, Yelahanka, Bengaluru-560064; borewell analysis dated 15.02.2022 shows Manganese exceeding standard)

hazardous_waste.facility_status: No integrated TSDF and no Sanitary Landfill Facility within Bengaluru Urban district; only 02 standalone incinerators exist. Hazardous waste generated by the 1718 industries is disposed through authorized TSDF, incinerators and recyclers (located outside the district) via MoU, monitored by KSPCB. KSPCB runs an E-manifest system (described as 'first in India') for tracking HW generation, collection, transport, treatment and disposal. No separate DOMESTIC hazardous-waste collection centres exist; domestic HW is segregated at dry-waste collection centres in BBMP/ULBs.
hazardous_waste.page: DEP 2022, printed p.45 (PDF page 48); section 'V. Hazardous Waste Management'. Note: the incinerable + landfillable + recyclable rows (12963.63 + 16429.38 + 45023.44 = 74416.45) sum to ~74416.45 vs the stated total 74416.29; a ~0.16 MT/annum rounding discrepancy in the source.
hazardous_waste.notes: All six numeric figures (1718, 74416.29, 12963.63, 16429.38, 45023.44) plus TSDF=Nil, SLF=Nil, incinerators=02, contaminated sites=1 were confirmed against the 200 dpi page image. The three sub-quantities do not exactly sum to the stated total (off by ~0.16 MT/annum) - reproduced verbatim; this is a source-document rounding artefact, not an extraction error.

figures.no_of_CBMWTF_in_inventory_table: -- (left blank / not stated in the at-a-glance inventory table)
figures.HCE_authorization_breakdown_2020_21_annu: Out of 10310 HCEs: 9216 authorized; 1220 had not applied for renewal; component HCF counts - Bedded hospitals/nursing homes 1532, Clinics/dispensaries 7115, Veterinary 188, Animal houses 0 (to be obtained from BBMP), Pathological labs 658, Blood banks 15, Clinical establishments 704, Research institutions 29, AYUSH 69

biomedical_waste.facility_status: The at-a-glance inventory table leaves 'No. of CBWTFs', 'Capacity' and 'No. of Deep burials' BLANK ('--'). However the gaps-and-action-plan section states BMW generated in the district is disposed through 5 CBMWTF: (1) M/s Medicare Environmental Management Pvt Ltd, (2) Maridi Bio Industries Pvt Ltd (Kanakapura Road, Ramanagar), (3) Meera Envirotech (Kolar), (4) Prajwal (on proximity principle), (5) Karnataka Waste Management Projects (Ramky Enviro Engineers). The district is described as having adequate facility; quantity generated equals quantity treated (37.321 Tons/day). Bar-code / QR-code tracking and GPS-fitted collection vehicles are in use.
biomedical_waste.page: DEP 2022, printed p.40 (PDF page 43) for the inventory table 'Inventory of BMW in the District'; the 5 named CBMWTFs and the 10310-HCE / 1220-unrenewed / 538.733 MT Covid figures are in the gaps section on printed p.40-p.42 (PDF pages 43-45).
biomedical_waste.notes: Inventory-table figures (1559 bedded, 8877 non-bedded, 9216 authorized, 37.321 Tons/day generated and treated, and the '--' blanks for CBWTF count/capacity/deep-burial) were confirmed against the 200 dpi page image. NOTE TWO INTERNAL TENSIONS in the source: (a) the inventory table lists CBWTFs as '--' (blank) yet the gaps text names 5 CBMWTFs serving the district - the '--' is best read as 'no CBMWTF located inside Bengaluru Urban district' (the 5 named facilities are in Ramanagar/Kolar/proximity locations). (b) HCF total counts differ across tables: inventory table = 1559 bedded + 8877 non-bedded = 10436 total, while the gaps text quotes a 2020-21 annual-report total of 10310 HCEs (1532 bedded + 7115 + 188 + 0 + 658 + 15 + 704 + 29 + 69 = 10310). Both reproduced verbatim; the difference is between annual-report vintages within the same document.

figures.user_fee: Rs.134/- per Ton charged by BBMP (user fee not yet fixed by the smaller ULBs)

cnd_waste.facility_status: District HAS access to a C&D recycling facility. Existing: M/s Rock Crystal (private) C&D waste processing facility, 1000 MTPD capacity, near Chikkajala, serving BBMP. Under construction: a second C&D plant awarded through BBMP, 750 TPD capacity at Kannur - reported as 'being set up and shall be operational in another 6 months' (i.e. ~late 2022 from a May-2022 document). NO C&D recycling facility at the smaller ULBs (Anekal/Attibele/Bommasandra/Chandapura/Hebbagodi/Jigani). C&D waste management is described as being practised by only one agency, in BBMP limits. Government agencies (BMRCL, PWD, BDA, BWSSB) directed to supply C&D waste to the Chikkajala processing facility.
cnd_waste.page: DEP 2022, printed p.36 (PDF page 39) for the C&D generation table and the recycling-facility status; the Rock Crystal 1000 MTPD / Kannur 750 TPD and the Rs.134/Ton user fee are repeated in the gaps section on printed p.37-p.38 (PDF pages 40-41).
cnd_waste.notes: The full per-ULB breakdown (BBMP 2500, Anekal 1.5, Attibele 0.5, Bommasandra 1.0, Chandapura 1.5, Hebbagodi 1.5, Jigani 1.0) and the Total 2507 TPD were confirmed against the 200 dpi page image. The prior-work figures are CONFIRMED: 'M/s Rock Crystal 1000 MTPD' (the document says MTPD, near Chikkajala, private, existing) and '750 TPD plant at Kannur' (awarded through BBMP, under construction). The 750 TPD plant's stated '6 months' timeline is relative to the May-2022 document and may now be operational - status not verifiable from this source.

extraction_caveats: All headline figures were image-verified at 200 dpi against the source PDF page, not just trusted from pdftotext.

Hazardous-waste sub-quantities (incinerable 12963.63 + landfillable 16429.38 + recyclable 45023.44 = 74416.45) do not exactly equal the stated total 74416.29 MT/annum; a ~0.16 MT/annum source rounding artefact, reproduced verbatim.

Biomedical: the at-a-glance inventory table records CBWTFs / capacity / deep-burials as '--' (blank), while the gaps text names 5 CBMWTFs serving the district (located in Ramanagar / Kolar / proximity). Best interpretation: zero CBMWTF physically inside Bengaluru Urban district, served by 5 external facilities. Flag for human confirmation.

Biomedical: HCF totals differ within the document - inventory table 1559 bedded + 8877 non-bedded = 10436, vs gaps-section 2020-21 annual-report total of 10310 HCEs. Different annual-report vintages; both reproduced.

C&D: the prior-work figures are confirmed - Rock Crystal 1000 MTPD (note: document states MTPD, near Chikkajala, private, existing) and 750 TPD at Kannur (awarded via BBMP, under construction as of May 2022, '6 months' to operational). Current operational status of the Kannur plant cannot be verified from this 2022 source.

Granularity: all three streams are reported DISTRICT-wide. Yelahanka is not a separate ULB row in any of these three tables (it sits within BBMP limits); its only stream-specific appearance is as the Mavallipura contaminated dumpsite under hazardous waste. BBMP figures effectively carry the BBMP+Yelahanka load.

Page citations use the document's printed footer label ('Page | N' = printed p.N). Printed p.N = PDF page N+3. HW table = printed p.45 / PDF p.48; BMW inventory = printed p.40 / PDF p.43; C&D table = printed p.36 / PDF p.39.
